title: Finite direct image and evaluation biduality for potential complexes
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, $r\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$. Schemes below are Noetherian excellent schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Use pinned potential dualizing complexes for dimension functions [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex], the bounded constructible small etale category $D^b_c$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and $D_K=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,K)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Write $\eta_M:M\to D_K^2M$ for the transpose of evaluation after symmetry of the tensor factors. Let $p:Y\to X$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], choose a dimension function $\delta_X$ and a pinned potential $K_X$, and use $\delta_Y=\delta_X\circ p$ and the pinned potential $K_Y=p^!K_X$ (the exceptional pullback right adjoint to finite direct image). Suppose $D_X$ and $D_Y$ preserve bounded constructible complexes. Then finite direct image $p_*$ is exact and conservative on etale $\Lambda$-module sheaves, and for every $M\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$ the finite-duality adjunction gives an isomorphism $$p_*D_YM\cong D_Xp_*M.$$ Its iteration identifies $p_*D_Y^2M$ with $D_X^2p_*M$ and identifies $p_*\eta_M$ with $\eta_{p_*M}$. Consequently $$p_*\mathcal H^q(D_Y^2M)\cong\mathcal H^q(D_X^2p_*M)$$ for every integer $q$. If $p$ is surjective, the unit $\Lambda_X\to p_*\Lambda_Y$ is a monomorphism.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Proposition 6.3.1 and Lemma 6.5.3; the unit monomorphism is used in the last paragraph of 6.5

proof.text: Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-stalk-formula] to the underlying abelian sheaf of a $\Lambda$-module sheaf $E$: $(p_*E)_{\bar x}=\prod_{\bar y\in Y_{\bar x}}E_{\bar y}$. This identification is $\Lambda$-linear, since each projection is restriction followed by taking a germ. By [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], $p_*$ is exact on the underlying abelian sheaves. Kernels and cokernels of module-sheaf maps are their abelian-sheaf kernels and cokernels with the induced scalar action, so it is exact on module sheaves too. If $p_*u$ is an isomorphism, the finite product of the stalk maps $u_{\bar y}$ over each $\bar x$ is an isomorphism. Each factor map is then an isomorphism (its kernel and cokernel are factors of the zero kernel and cokernel of the product). Every geometric point of $Y$ occurs over its composite geometric point of $X$. Thus [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] says $u$ is an isomorphism. This proves conservativity without assuming $p$ surjective.

By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], exact $p_*$ on module sheaves computes its derived functor termwise on every complex. In particular it commutes with cohomology: for a representative $C^\bullet$, applying $p_*$ to $\ker d^q/\operatorname{im}d^{q-1}$ gives $\ker p_*d^q/\operatorname{im}p_*d^{q-1}$. Finite direct image preserves constructible abelian sheaves on a Noetherian base by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-constructible-noetherian]. For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^r$, the module structure is the uniquely induced scalar action on an abelian sheaf killed by $\ell^r$, so finite locally constant abelian restrictions are exactly finite locally constant $\Lambda$-module restrictions. Consequently $F=p_*$ sends $D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$ to $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$, preserving the cohomology interval. The assumed preservation by $D_Y$ makes both $M$ and $D_YM$ bounded below, as required in the next application.

We fix tensor--Hom transposition on the ordinary etale derived categories, with all tensor products over $\Lambda$ and derived. Applying $H^0$ of derived global sections to the currying isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction], and then using [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections], gives the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(B,R\mathcal Hom(A,K))=\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes A,K)$. Define $e_A:D_KA\otimes A\to K$ as the image of $1_{D_KA}$. Thus the transpose of $v:B\to D_KA$ is $e_A(v\otimes1_A)$, by naturality in $B$. Evaluation naturality is the same bijection's naturality in $A$: $e_A(D_Ka\otimes1_A)=e_B(1_{D_KB}\otimes a)$ for $a:A\to B$. With the canonical symmetry $\sigma$ of [lem-kun-tensor-sym], the stipulated bidual map satisfies exactly $e_{D_KA}(\eta_A\otimes1_{D_KA})=e_A\sigma_{A,D_KA}$. These are identities of morphisms; no biduality isomorphism is assumed.

source.place: Tags 08J9, lemma-internal-hom, and 08JA, lemma-section-RHom-over-U; evaluation of the currying bijection at an identity

proof.text: Use the canonical derived adjunction $p^{-1}\dashv F$ of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and write $c_A:p^{-1}FA\to A$ for its counit. Define $\mu_{A,B}:FA\otimes FB\to F(A\otimes B)$ to be the adjoint of $c_A\otimes c_B$, using the inverse-image tensor isomorphism of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]. Naturality follows by transposing and using $c_{A'}p^{-1}F(a)=a c_A$ in each factor. Moreover $F(\sigma_{A,B})\mu_{A,B}=\mu_{B,A}\sigma_{FA,FB}$: after transposition both sides are $\sigma_{A,B}(c_A\otimes c_B)$. Here inverse image commutes with the tensor symmetry: on representatives both swaps send a tensor in bidegree $(i,j)$ to $(-1)^{ij}$ times its reverse, and termwise inverse image preserves that scalar. The symmetry is the signed symmetry of [lem-kun-tensor-sym]. This specifies, and checks the only properties needed of, the product map; it does not assert that $\mu$ is invertible.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 6.3.1, finite-direct-image weak-reflexivity comparison; agent expansion of the ordinary adjunction product map

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-finite-exceptional-internal-hom] with $f=p$, $N=K_X$, and $A=M$, or $A=D_YM$. Its hypotheses hold: $\Lambda$ is finite commutative, both schemes are Noetherian, $p$ is finite, $K_X\in D^+$ by [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex], and these two choices of $A$ are bounded below by the assumption on $D_Y$. The specified identification $K_Y=p^!K_X$ gives natural isomorphisms $\chi_A:FD_YA\xrightarrow{\sim}D_XFA$. Put $t:FK_Y\to K_X$ for the exceptional counit. The cited theorem also identifies $p$ as compactifiable, $Rp_!=F$, and $p^!K_X=p^\times K_X$, compatibly with this counit, so [lem-asd-internal-adjunction-evaluation] applies with $Q=FD_YA$ and $h=1$. The transpose of $\chi_A$ is $t F(e_A(c_{D_YA}\otimes1_A))\Pi_{p,Q,A}$. By [lem-amb-tensor-projection-adjunct] and naturality of the ordinary counit, $F(c_{D_YA}\otimes1_A)\Pi_{p,Q,A}=\mu_{D_YA,A}$: their ordinary adjoints are both $c_{D_YA}\otimes c_A$. Hence the precise normalization we use is
$$e_{FA}(\chi_A\otimes1_{FA})=t F(e_A)\mu_{D_YA,A}.$$
The evaluations on the left and right use $K_X$ and $K_Y$, respectively.

source.place: XVII, Proposition 6.3.1, finite-map comparison; the evaluation--counit normalization is expanded using the existing internal-adjunction nodes

proof.text:
Set $a=\chi_M:FD_YM\to D_XFM$ and $b=\chi_{D_YM}:FD_Y^2M\to D_XFD_YM$. Since internal Hom is a functor in its first variable, $D_Xa:D_X^2FM\to D_XFD_YM$ is an isomorphism. Therefore the iterated comparison, with its variance made explicit, is
$$\beta_M=(D_Xa)^{-1}b:FD_Y^2M\xrightarrow{\sim}D_X^2FM.$$
This uses the two isomorphisms supplied in Step 5 and functoriality of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom].

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.5.3: iteration of the finite-map internal-Hom comparison

proof.text:
We check the actual bidual maps by transposing maps $FM\to D_XFD_YM$. Write $\mu=\mu_{M,D_YM}$. Steps 3--5 give the transpose of $b F\eta_M$ as the following three equal expressions:
$$t F(e_{D_YM})\mu_{D_Y^2M,D_YM}(F\eta_M\otimes1)
=t F(e_{D_YM}(\eta_M\otimes1))\mu
=t F(e_M)\mu_{D_YM,M}\sigma_{FM,FD_YM}.$$
The first equality is naturality of $\mu$ in its first factor; the second uses the defining identity for $\eta_M$ from Step 3 followed by the symmetry identity of Step 4. On the other hand, evaluation naturality from Step 3 says that the transpose of $(D_Xa)\eta_{FM}$ is
$$e_{FM}(a\otimes1_{FM})\sigma_{FM,FD_YM},$$
which is exactly the last expression by the normalization in Step 5. Transposition is injective, so $b F\eta_M=(D_Xa)\eta_{FM}$. Multiplication by $(D_Xa)^{-1}$ now gives $\beta_M F\eta_M=\eta_{FM}$. This verifies compatibility with the evaluation-transpose maps, rather than merely comparing their source and target objects.

source.place: XVII, proof of Proposition 6.3.1: explicit evaluation/symmetry calculation for compatibility with weak reflexivity; Lemma 6.5.3

proof.text: Apply $\mathcal H^q$ to the isomorphism $\beta_M$ of Step 6. The termwise calculation in Step 2 identifies its source with $p_*\mathcal H^q(D_Y^2M)$ and its target with $\mathcal H^q(D_X^2p_*M)$. This gives the required isomorphism for every $q\in\mathbf Z$. The identification uses only the kernel/image description of cohomology in [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and exactness, so includes negative degrees and commutes with the maps checked in Step 7.

source.place: XVII, Lemma 6.5.3, displayed canonical cohomology isomorphism, printed p.299

proof.text: Finally assume $p$ is surjective. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-geometric-stalk], the stalk of $\Lambda_X$ at $\bar x$ is $\Lambda$. The finite stalk formula of Step 1 identifies the target stalk with $\prod_{\bar y\in Y_{\bar x}}\Lambda$. The unit sends a constant local section $\lambda$ to its pullback constant section, whose germ at every $\bar y$ is $\lambda$; its stalk is therefore the diagonal map $\lambda\mapsto(\lambda)_{\bar y}$. The fibre is nonempty by surjectivity, so projection to any factor is a left inverse to this diagonal. It is injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-detect-mono] to the underlying abelian sheaf map: all its geometric stalks are injective, hence it is a monomorphism. The same holds as a module-sheaf map since a zero kernel is detected on the underlying abelian sheaf.
